pll1d42c1-d1e3501.summary: Turns to omnipotence and asks whether God is truly omnipotent because he can do all things or because he can do what he wills.

pll1d42c1-d1e3504.summary: States that many authorities prove God can do all things.

pll1d42c1-d1e3507.summary: Cites the Quaestiones veteris et novi Testamenti (attributed to Augustine): God can do all things but does only what fits his truth and justice.
claims: God can do all but does only what fits his truth and justice.

pll1d42c1-d1e3528.summary: Further: God could have made all things at once, but reason, that is his will, forbade, since God's will is reasonable and most just. So God can do all things.
claims: God could have made all at once.

pl-l1d42c1.summary: Begins the treatment of omnipotence: is God omnipotent because he can do all things, or only what he wills? Many authorities show he can do all things: Augustine says God can do all things but does only what fits his truth and justice, and could have made all things at once but reason, that is his reasonable and just will, prevented it.
claims: God does only what fits his truth and justice.
God's will is reasonable and just.
